A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

task shifting of AMTLS has thus far been studied in the context of administration of uterotonincs (misoprostols or oxytocin) by CHWs and auxilary midwives and has resulted in a reduction in PPH, high levels of appropriate use and high levels of satisfaction among users.
task shifting of AMTLS is feasible and effective in preventing postpartum haemorrhage, and is acceptable by women and their partners.
task shifting of specific AMSTL components is feasible and safe, but further evaluation is required for uterine massage, controlled cord traction and postpartum tonicity assessment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
task shifting of uterotonic administration to unskilled providers is feasible, safe and acceptable.
task shifting of the provision of uterine tonics is a feasible strategy to increase access of women to potentially life-saving uterotonics.
task shifting of uterotonic drugs is a safe and feasible intervention that could potentially reduce the burden of PPH.
